narrative.title: Why Kelsey?
narrative.highlight: Healthcare sales depends on trust, clinical credibility, and follow-through. I built client trust managing institutional accounts at Goldman Sachs, earned clinical credibility training in the ER as a licensed EMT, and showed follow-through in bilingual territory outreach.
narrative.body:
My career started in client relationship management and business development. My longstanding interest in medicine led me to earn my EMT license, where training in the field and ER alongside clinicians gave me firsthand insight into clinical practice and the potential for advances in life sciences and medical technology to transform treatment. That experience clarified how I wanted to make an impact in healthcare by helping bring innovative therapies and devices to more patients through partnerships with the physicians who make treatment decisions.

Although I have not held a pharmaceutical or medical device sales title, I bring a proven track record of building client relationships, generating business, and retaining high-value accounts, alongside firsthand healthcare experience. At Goldman Sachs, I managed approximately 20 multi-million-dollar accounts, maintaining 100% client retention while navigating complex client needs. Through 18 months of volunteer Spanish-language territory outreach, I developed skills in prospecting, objection handling, and persuasive communication, generating more than 50% of new commitments through referrals. My EMT training strengthened my clinical understanding and experience collaborating with healthcare professionals, preparing me to communicate clinical information effectively, engage physicians, and drive measurable territory growth.

startStories.title: Account Management and Client Retention
startStories.teaser: At Goldman Sachs I managed about 20 multi-million-dollar lending accounts and kept every one of them, with zero escalations.
startStories.body:
At Goldman Sachs I managed about 20 multi-million-dollar corporate lending accounts. The contracts ran 100 to 250+ pages, and I read every one front to back so I'd catch a problem before the client did. If I gave a client a deadline, I met it, even when that meant working from a plane on Christmas Eve. When teammates were out, I covered their accounts too.

In sales terms, that's account management and customer retention. I kept 100% of my book with zero escalations by knowing the details cold, communicating complex terms clearly, and following through every time. That's how I'll build trust with physicians and protect the accounts in my territory.

startStories.title: Clinical Credibility
startStories.teaser: I finished my UT Dallas EMT program in the top 5% of my class and trained alongside physicians, nurses, and trauma teams.
startStories.body:
I finished the UT Dallas EMT program in the top 5% of my cohort. One night around 2am, I was sent to the helipad with two nurses to receive an air ambulance patient. When we got him to the trauma bay, the physician called for someone to cut his clothes off. I stepped in while he performed an emergency tracheotomy, and the nurses told the other students to follow my lead.

That's where my clinical credibility comes from. I understand clinical workflows and patient handoffs, and I know what happens when a product adds a step. With that background I can hold a real conversation with a physician, communicate clinical value, and position a product around patient outcomes.

startStories.title: Business Acumen and Data-Driven Insight
startStories.teaser: At Vivint I found seven operational inefficiencies that added up to a $2 million revenue opportunity.
startStories.body:
I started at Vivint without knowing SQL and was delivering executive reporting in nine days. Once I was in the data every day, I noticed things nobody had asked me to look for. I found seven operational inefficiencies that added up to a $2 million revenue opportunity, built the business case, and presented it to senior leadership. They used it to reallocate resources.

For a territory, that means market analysis and KPI tracking. I'll know my numbers, spot growth opportunities in my accounts, and bring my manager and customers a clear business case.

startStories.title: Territory Outreach and Bilingual Communication
startStories.teaser: In a Spanish-speaking territory across Nebraska, Iowa, and South Dakota, more than half of my new commitments came from referrals.
startStories.body:
For 18 months I did volunteer outreach in a Spanish-speaking territory across Nebraska, Iowa, and South Dakota. One community leader controlled access to local families, and he had shut out every representative before me. I didn't push. I got to know his wife first, learned he missed playing soccer, and organized a pickup game. Over time he became my best source of referrals.

That's prospecting and objection handling with a hard-to-reach stakeholder. I used pre-call planning and post-call reviews, hit my assigned quotas, and generated more than 50% of new commitments through referrals. I'll use the same approach with physicians who have already turned other reps away.

startStories.title: Coaching and Onboarding
startStories.teaser: I mentored an intern and two struggling teammates at Goldman Sachs, and trained a new representative while we hit our goals 12 weeks in a row.
startStories.body:
At Goldman Sachs I mentored an intern and two teammates who were struggling. With each one, I figured out whether the gap was knowledge, confidence, or process before I tried to fix anything. As a volunteer representative, I onboarded a new rep, and we met our weekly goals 12 weeks in a row while I trained her.

In a sales role, that carries over to training office staff on a new product, working cross-functionally, and eventually helping onboard new reps on my team. I measure success by results, not activity.

startStories.title: Referral-Based Business Development
startStories.teaser: I built a paid private school admissions consulting practice to 13 families, all through referrals.
startStories.body:
In 2023 I started a consulting practice helping Dallas families with private school admissions. I set my own pricing and built every consultation around the family's needs. All 13 families came through referrals, with no paid marketing or cold outreach. Several came back for a younger child, and one student I worked with was admitted to a school with a 15% acceptance rate.

That's business development from zero. I ran needs assessments, delivered results, and earned repeat business and referrals. That's the same way I'll grow a territory.
